reuse.why: getNextDate, getUpcomingDates, the new getDatesInRange and the budget schedule template all go through the single shared applyWeekendRule, and the new handler reuses recurConfigToRSchedule and RSchedule.

duplication.why: The weekend, holiday and daily-skip rule is defined once; what remains is the template's outer skipWeekend ternary, repeated twice, and two small local wrappers around applyWeekendRule.

placement.why: The rule sits in shared/schedules.ts and the handler in schedules/app.ts as the tree does; the parse-and-format wrappers in schedule-template are local rather than shared.

scope.why: Every change serves the five steps; the field rename weekendSolve to weekendSolveMode in parseRecurDate aligns the RSchedule data with the rule type and is justified.

maintainability.why: One rule object passed to one function is easy to evolve; the look-ahead sizes (count*7 plus the holiday count, and 2 + 3 per holiday days of padding) are heuristic magic numbers, and the redundant outer gating in schedule-template could drift.

bypasses_abstraction.where: budget/schedule-template.ts createScheduleList still wraps the call in its own `dateConditions.value.skipWeekend ? getAdjustedOccurrence(...) : nextBaseDate` ternary, which re-decides whether the rule applies when applyWeekendRule already does.

disguised_duplication.where: No logic is copied under another shape; getAdjustedOccurrence and isSkippedOccurrence are thin adapters over applyWeekendRule.

abstraction_drift.where: applyWeekendRule(date, rule) keeps one rule-object parameter, and its frequency and holidays fields carry the daily-skip and holiday steps without extra flags; the two createScheduleList sites in schedule-template.ts still gate on skipWeekend themselves.
